Transitions and animations

W3C CSS Snapshot 2026

CSS can make a change happen gradually. A transition responds to a change in value. An animation follows a named sequence of steps.

Open interactive lesson

Transition a changed value

Set transition on the base rule so it applies as a state starts and ends. The first value names the property; the second sets the duration. The hover or focus rule provides the new value.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Transition a changed value</title>
  <style>
    button { background: lightblue; transition: background-color 250ms; }
    button:hover, button:focus-visible { background: gold; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<button type="button">View product</button>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Hover or Tab to the button. The background changes gradually over a quarter of a second.

Define animation steps with @keyframes

@keyframes names a sequence and gives it values at points in time. from is the start and to is the end. animation connects the sequence to the element and sets a duration.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Define animation steps with @keyframes</title>
  <style>
    .notice { animation: appear 800ms; }
    @keyframes appear { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<p class="notice">Your order is ready.</p>
<p>Your package is on the way.</p>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Reload to see the first paragraph fade in once. The other paragraph is visible immediately.

Respect a reduced-motion preference

Some users set their system to reduce motion. The prefers-reduced-motion media feature can detect that preference. Remove an optional effect while leaving the content available.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Respect a reduced-motion preference</title>
  <style>
    .notice { animation: appear 1s; }
    @keyframes appear { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .notice { animation: none; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<p class="notice">Your order is ready.</p>
<p>Your package is on the way.</p>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Enable reduced motion in the system or emulate it in DevTools and reload. The notice appears immediately.
